source_review.notes: Checked all seven structured references. Current official gRPC deadlines documentation supports explicit deadlines, remaining-time propagation, language variation, and handler responsibility; cancellation guidance supports cooperative stop-work; metadata and PROTOCOL-HTTP2 support initial/trailing placement, reserved/binary keys, timeout grammar, duplicate/order caveats, and suggested header limits. Interceptor/authentication guidance supports per-call middleware and dedicated credential APIs. W3C Trace Context and RFC 9113 supply current trace and HTTP/2 context.

evidence: Checked D, t, r, B(t), e_i, w_i, C_i, metadata multimap K, identity I, untrusted metadata U, and terminal T(c) for consistent domains.
Confirmed max/min budget expressions, monotonicity inequalities, cancellation implication counterexample, and interceptor composition are syntactically and semantically consistent.
Confirmed timeout, deadline, remaining budget, cancellation, call context, metadata, trailers, interceptors, and baggage are defined.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation distinguishes time budget, resource policy, metadata trust, and domain effects.

evidence: Recomputed 1000-150-150=700 ms and the later zero boundary max(0,1000-980-50)=0.
Recomputed Exercise 2 allocations as 1600 ms then 900 ms, below the 1000 ms minimum useful database time.
Checked the wire timeout value maximum of eight digits, six documented units, and suggested 8 KiB header defaults against the official protocol/docs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All numbers are exact examples or attributed protocol constants; no empirical latency prediction is claimed.

evidence: Derived 0 ≤ B_{i+1} ≤ B_i from nonnegative elapsed/reserve, max at zero, and child cap minimum.
Checked retry/backoff/queue time consumes rather than resets the same B(t).
Constructed commit-before-cancel trace proving cancellation does not imply zero effects.
Checked metadata forwarding preserves bytes but cannot establish authentication truth without a verified binding.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Symbolic claims are bounded by clock, estimate, runtime propagation, and trust assumptions stated in the chapter.

evidence: Reviewed missing, already-expired, extremely short, long-stream, clock-adjusted, rounded, retried, hedged, queued, fanned-out, and proxy-limited calls.
Reviewed cancellation before/after dispatch, child start, commit, durable handoff, response, and cleanup plus detached/uncooperative work.

Reviewed metadata casing, duplicates, ASCII/binary, reserved names, size limits, spoofed identity, token leakage, trailer stripping, interceptor bypass/order, baggage fan-out, and authorization changes.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans time, concurrency, persistence, protocol, intermediary, privacy, and adversarial trust boundaries.

evidence: The remaining-deadline-budget model checks nonnegative remaining time, a capped child allocation, admission threshold, and zero late boundary.
Confirmed no hop/retry resets budget and every cancellation path separates stop-work from committed effects.
Confirmed metadata is bounded, allowlisted, redacted, and authenticated identity is separated from untrusted caller claims.
Confirmed durable jobs acquire explicit ownership and gRPC terminal status/trailers remain distinct from domain outcome.
invariant_checking.notes: Local arithmetic demonstrates the invariant; real runtime clocks, propagation, proxies, credentials, and cleanup require specified integration evidence.

evidence: Reviewed budget-monotonicity proof and confirmed nonnegative elapsed/reserve/cap premises are used.
Reviewed commit-before-cancellation counterexample and confirmed it refutes rollback inference without overclaiming all cancellations commit.
Reviewed untrusted-role metadata counterexample and confirmed infrastructure forwarding alone supplies no issuer/audience/principal proof.
proof_review.notes: The chapter's proof arguments are valid and explicitly scoped.

evidence: Confirmed deadline is labeled caller intent/resource budget, not a completion guarantee.
Confirmed cancellation is a cooperative signal, not rollback/preemption/execution evidence.
Confirmed protocol metadata mechanics, runtime/language variation, application policy, and domain-message semantics are separated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Models, mechanisms, implementation behavior, policy, guarantees, and evidence remain distinct.

evidence: Background snippet verification records the deterministic budget execution under artifacts/snippets/API-054/report.json before promotion.
Current protocol constants and behaviors are attributed to official sources with retrieval date.
Live latency, clock behavior, runtimes, proxy trailers, metadata limits, credentials, traces, cancellation cleanup, and durable workflows remain case-specific evidence obligations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production gRPC chain, credential system, proxy, workload, or incident was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed deadline/budget derivation, admission, cancellation cooperation, transaction/workflow outcome, wire encoding, metadata placement, message-versus-metadata ownership, interceptor order, tracing/baggage, credential protection, status/trailers, and adversarial verification as one coherent gRPC context model.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through monotonic remaining-time APIs, reserves/caps/admission, structured cancellation/cleanup, idempotent recovery, durable handoff, metadata registry and size/redaction rules, supported credentials, explicit interceptor order, trace allowlists, proxy trailer tests, and cancellation-to-work-stop telemetry.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module moves from time-budget first principles through cancellation/effects, wire propagation, metadata/trust, middleware, observability, and evidence. Ten examples are distinct and five exercises progress from definitions to emergency-dispatch transfer with complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
